hypothesis: For the declared two-spin Poisson model fixtures, a PT eligibility guard rejects deterministic-positive interactions that an even-arity-only transfer would accept. At least one such rejected fixture has expected finite-N pressure exceeding the transferred zero-message replica-symmetric upper value by more than0.01 nats per spin. All symmetric-sign and zero-interaction controls satisfy that old finite-N upper inequality within declared numerical tolerances. Two independently organized expectations agree.

input.kind: synthetic applicability and certificate-boundary audit; not a decoder benchmark

input.exposure: Manuscript and original PT statement read before registration. Two-spin Poisson-thinning formulas reasoned about analytically before execution; this is nonblind applicability calibration, not a newly discovered counterexample to a theorem.

baseline: Naive transfer checks even arity and first moments only and treats B0=log2+alpha*E logcosh(beta J) as a finite-N upper certificate for all fixtures. Guarded transfer additionally checks the exact signed-moment eligibility for these bounded three specified sign laws. The guard is not a general algorithm deciding all moment inequalities for arbitrary input distributions.
judge: OracleA averages the literal four-spin-configuration partition function using a dynamic distribution of the loop/cross score sums conditional on the original Poisson interaction count. OracleB uses independent Poisson-thinned cross-coupling counts and the separately expected linear loop contribution. Bound discarded count tails using the Poisson mass and first-moment tail, and repeat transcendental calculations at the declared higher precision. Neither oracle samples the Gibbs state or uses the target upper bound as its expected pressure.
failure: Any oracle disagreement or tail budget violation, any accepted-control upper-inequality violation beyond the combined tail/arithmetic allowance, incorrect declared sign-law eligibility, or absence of a rejected fixture with excess greater than0.01. Preserve unfavorable results; do not expand the grid after seeing outputs to meet the threshold.
metrics: expected finite-N pressure from both organizations
limits: This audits a model-transfer precondition and the older PT finite-N upper bound, not the2026 all-depth variational equality. Deterministic positive J is intentionally outside the sufficient signed-moment class; a failed transferred inequality does not refute the manuscript or the ferromagnetic model. N=2 with replacement is a literal mathematical fixture, not evidence about thermodynamic convergence, a physical mesh, LDPC channels, regular code graphs, solver speed, decoding thresholds, SAT/UNSAT thresholds, or engineering deployment. Old PT hypotheses already specify this boundary; no incremental benefit of the new theorem is claimed. Analytic tail bounds and numerical arithmetic checks have different evidence status.
